title: Next.js vs React
description: Compare plain React with Next.js – what extra features do you get and when to use each.

slides.title: React Alone ⚛️
slides.content:
# Vanilla React (CRA / Vite)

* A JavaScript library for building user interfaces.
* You must manually configure routing, SSR, code splitting, image optimisation, etc.
* Typically renders on the client (CSR).
* Great for single‑page applications (SPAs) where SEO isn't critical.

slides.title: Next.js – The Framework 🏗️
slides.content:
# Next.js Adds

* **Routing** (file‑system based)
* **Pre‑rendering** (SSG, SSR, ISR)
* **API Routes** – backend endpoints without a separate server.
* **Image and Font Optimisation**
* **Middleware**
* **SEO** out of the box (metadata, head management)
* **Built‑in CSS Support** (CSS Modules, Sass)

quizData.question: For a public e‑commerce site that needs good SEO, which would you choose?
quizData.explanation: E‑commerce sites need SEO and fast load times. Next.js provides server‑rendered HTML that search engines can crawl easily.

slides.title: Code Comparison
slides.content: React (CRA) vs Next.js – fetching data for a page.

quizData.question: In the Next.js example, what is the key advantage of `getStaticProps`?

options.text: It fetches data at build time, so the page is pre‑rendered with data

quizData.explanation: `getStaticProps` runs at build time on the server. The HTML is generated with the data already present, no client‑side loading spinner.

slides.title: Key Decision 🤔
slides.content: Use **plain React** for internal dashboards, real‑time apps with heavy client‑side state. Use **Next.js** for any website where performance, SEO, or routing convenience matters. Most new projects start with Next.js because you can still do everything React can do.
